A specific texture associated with the event

I drift off into a world of my own
make sure never to be alone with another person

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
When the memory comes back it feels completely real across all my senses at once

You can never know who will harm you

Having strong physical reactions when something reminded you of the stressful experience
Being superalert or watchful or on guard

issues.item: Threat: missing/none selected despite multiple current-danger and exposure-related items
issues.explanation: The profile contains several items implying an active sense of present threat or exposure (e.g., 'World is Dangerous', 'Exposed to Others', concealment to avoid being noticed), yet the Threat component is entirely absent. For this trauma type, such items would usually cohere with at least some explicit threat content; the omission makes the cross-node picture clinically uneven.

'World is Dangerous' expresses a broad ongoing threat belief, but the formulation specifies no active links into or out of Threat and no Threat items are endorsed. This makes the appraisal sit awkwardly in the formulation because it functions more like a threat belief than an isolated negative self-appraisal.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Concealing Clothing: wear concealing clothing to avoid being noticed
issues.explanation: 'Concealing Clothing ... to avoid being noticed' implies active management of current interpersonal threat/visibility. With Threat completely unrepresented and no Trigger→Threat or Maladaptive Strategies→Threat linkage in the formulation, this strategy lacks a clear matching symptom target in the rest of the profile.

issues.item: Threat from Strangers: I feel threatened by strangers approaching me even in ordinary situations
issues.explanation: The Threat node is not clinically coherent here. 'Flashbacks' and 'Physical Reactivity' are re-experiencing/arousal responses rather than threat appraisals, while the only genuine threat appraisal selected is 'Threat from Strangers.' That mixes different constructs within one node.

vignette: Tyler had grown accustomed to the darkness that crept in every night. As a housekeeper at a busy hotel, he often worked late shifts and would return home under the veil of evening shadows. But despite his familiarity with nighttime, it still unsettled him. He couldn't quite explain why, but something about the absence of light made him feel vulnerable, like an invisible presence was lurking just out of sight. As a child, Tyler had been physically abused by one of his caregivers. The memories were hazy, but certain details lingered – the scratchy texture of the carpet in the room where it happened, the muffled sounds of children crying from elsewhere in the house. Whenever he encountered these triggers, the past came flooding back. At work, Tyler struggled to cope with the sound of kids crying. It didn't matter if they were just upset about a lost toy or having a tantrum; to him, their wails transported him straight back to that dreaded room. He would hastily excuse himself and retreat to a quiet corner, trying to collect his thoughts before returning to his duties. Tyler's way of dealing with these overwhelming memories was to disengage from reality altogether. When the emotions became too much to bear, he would drift off into a world of his own – a fantasy escape where the pain and fear didn't exist. It was a fleeting reprieve, but it helped him get through the tough moments. As time went on, Tyler started to notice that he was dropping responsibilities more often. He would call in sick or leave work early without explanation, simply because he couldn't face the world outside his apartment. His colleagues grew concerned about his reliability, and his manager began to question his commitment to the job. Despite this, Tyler felt compelled to avoid being alone with others whenever possible. It wasn't that he didn't trust them; it's just that he believed people could see right through him, into the depths of his painful past. He imagined they could spot the scars – not physical ones, but the invisible marks left by years of abuse and neglect. In those quiet moments when Tyler was alone with his thoughts, memories replayed like a perpetual film loop in his mind. The sounds, sights, and sensations came flooding back, transporting him to that traumatic event all over again. When this happened, he would shut down entirely – unable to speak or think coherently until the memory had receded. Tyler couldn't shake off the feeling of being an object rather than a person. It was as if he'd lost control over his own life, and everyone around him saw only a shell of who he truly was. Even more terrifying, though, was the constant fear that lurked beneath – a nagging suspicion that anyone could harm him at any moment. Sometimes, without warning, Tyler would relive the traumatic experience in vivid detail. It wasn't just memories; it felt like his body and mind were reliving every second of that awful event all over again. The physical sensations left him gasping for breath – a familiar but intense response to the perceived threat. Tyler's world had become one of heightened alertness, where potential dangers lurked around every corner. He couldn't relax in public or quiet spaces; his senses were perpetually on high alert, waiting for something, anything, that might signal another attack. This state of hypervigilance left him exhausted – a tiredness not just physical but emotional as well. One evening, after an especially grueling shift at the hotel, Tyler stumbled upon an article about PTSD support groups in his local area. It was then he realized how suffocating his situation had become. Something within him stirred; for the first time in years, he felt a glimmer of hope that things could change – that with help, he might finally begin to heal and reclaim control over his life. Tyler's eyes locked onto the phone number at the bottom of the page as if it held the key to unlocking his freedom. With a hesitant determination, he reached for his phone and dialed, the first step toward seeking help after years of suffering in silence.
